S1Result: Playwright has a new only failures option. It can shrink a test report by about ninety five percent.
But the smaller report says that zero tests passed.
Two thousand tests. Twenty of them failed. The full report is three megabytes. With only failures, it is one hundred and fifty eight kilobytes.
Here is what you save, and what you lose.
S2Setup: The suite has two thousand tests. I made zero, twenty, one hundred, or four hundred of them fail.
Each run writes a report in one of three formats, with the option off, and with the option on.
With the two terminal reporters, that is one hundred and sixty runs. I recorded the report size and the run time of every one.
S3Size: With twenty failed tests, the first format drops from three megabytes to one hundred and fifty eight kilobytes.
The second drops from two hundred and fifty kilobytes to thirty four.
The web page report drops the least. From nine hundred and sixty four kilobytes to five hundred and ninety nine. The viewer app is inside the file.
And the run is not faster. The run time showed no consistent difference.
S4Kept: What counts as a failure? Tests that fail, tests that time out, and flaky tests that pass on a retry all stay in the report.
Passed tests and skipped tests are dropped.
S5Totals: Here is the catch. The totals shrink with the report.
In the full report, one thousand nine hundred and eighty tests passed. In the smaller report of the same run, zero passed.
The test count says twenty, not two thousand.
And a tool that reads test durations from the report got timings for zero tests.
S6Fix: So use only failures for the report a person opens after a red run.
Do not point a dashboard or a pass rate check at it.
If you need both, write blob reports and merge them twice. Once in full, and once with only failures.
One caveat. The suite uses no browser and no attachments. Measure your own reports before you rely on these numbers.
S7EndCard: Every run and every number is in the public repo. The links are in the description.
